description: Albion's lore, myths and places as its people tell them, from Living Server, rewritten.

lines.text: I still think Avalon was in the marsh the whole time and we just never found the door.
The isles did not find Avalon, they just pulled back the curtain.
Heard Lady Nimue walks the marsh at night because the door to Avalon is still out there.
The marsh mist sits in the same spots every night. Real fog moves.
Some say Merlin hid Avalon himself before he vanished, so nobody could loot it while he was away.
Anyone else think Avalon was hiding in the marsh all along?
A whole race of mages does not come from a city that is not there. Avalon was hidden, not missing.
The day the isles opened, half the Avalonians I knew went straight to the ruins like pilgrims.
Before the isles, the nearest thing Albion had to Avalon was a name on a swamp.
I have waited in the marsh half the night just to watch Lady Nimue go by. Worth it.
I get why explorers chase the Avalon story, but marsh slimes give awful experience.
The Stonecrush ogres eat granite. Think about what that does to a sword.
The heralds call Golestandt she, but half the raid stories I have heard still say he.
I dare anyone to go look at Golestandt and come back walking.
The Spirit of the Emperor, the Forgotten Emperor, Emperor Seleucus. That crypt has more emperors than Rome ever did.
Merlin is not dead. The barrow's empty, mark me.
Heard Wizard Lichas was Merlin's apprentice who stayed behind when the barrow was sealed.
Heard the stones were raised for Ambrosius Aurelianus. His shade is out there somewhere.
Merlin left his staff behind. Wizards do not leave their staff unless they mean to come back.
Touch the stones at Stonehenge for luck before a big raid. Half the realm does it.
A friend of mine conned Lady Nimue once. The color alone told him to walk away. Leave her be.
They say the lady of the lake kept the blade after Arthur, which is why we only have the scabbard.
Wherever Lady Nimue stops in the marsh at night is where I would start digging. I am convinced.
I dare you to follow Lady Nimue her whole route on foot without losing her.
Rode right past the Green Knight once. He nodded. I swear he nodded.
Heard the Green Knight's blade never drops. I have never met anyone with one.
The Afanc hatchlings mean there is a mother. Think about that next swim.
The Legendary Afanc has not left the lake since Arthur's day. Can you blame it.
I think Xanxicar was guarding Avalon long before the Drakoran came. Maybe that is why it stayed hidden.
The crystals down there hum when you stand still. Old Avalonians say it is the city singing.
Arawn sent the Inconnu because someone is stealing his dead. Strange allies, eyes like wells.
I have never heard an Inconnu laugh. Not once.
The Drakoran are not stupid beasts. They have mystics, medics and sawbones. That is an army.
Heard the Inconnu count every Albion death for Arawn.
Our relics are Merlin's staff and Excalibur's scabbard. Lose either and the Bards sing about it for a month.
The scabbard was always worth more than the blade. The old tales say it kept Arthur from bleeding.
The missing relic is Excalibur itself. Find the blade and you will find Avalon too. My theory anyway.
High Priest Andania still preaches to an empty temple. You have to admire it.
Every map of Albion ends in water, but the water does not end. Swim long enough and the world stops you.
I keep a map of every cave in Albion nobody talks about. It is longer than you would think.
Anyone else ever swum out past the last island just to see what happens?
The only word left in that journal was Golestandt. Makes you think.
The barrow of Merlin sits under Stonehenge, and I do not think he is in it.
Merlin's staff and the scabbard are ours. So where did Excalibur go?
Back then, we argued for hours about where Avalon was. Turns out it was right there the whole time.
